These probabilities are judgment-based priors from general MLP training behaviour. I did not run or look up any benchmark data.

- **High learning rate (3, 4, 21):** high learning rates tend to be unstable, so a larger batch, fewer layers or a lower learning rate should help more there than elsewhere.
- **Small width (22):** growing the width should help more when the network is narrow.
- **Depth step (16):** the step from 2 to 1 layers likely costs more than the step from 3 to 2.
- **Alpha steps and most other pairs:** alpha only matters at the large end of its grid, so most pairs are mostly N.
